parsed.why: Thin record; no trans criminalisation, but universal document mismatch with no remedy, protections omit gender identity, and majority stigma leave outed travellers exposed without documented enforcement.

Criminalised same-sex conduct, absolute monarchy, official hostility, banned organisations and no recognition/remedy; though sexuality law is secondary, it supplies police leverage, social licence and severe uncertainty.
No national trans crime, but birth-sex custody abuse, recent transfemicide pattern, Pride arrests, local expression bans and service exclusion outweigh protective patchwork and acceptance signals.

Decriminalised but no gender recognition, rejected marker changes, documented border-document friction, constitutional/discrimination gaps, official medicalisation, demonising coverage, and invisibility increase exposure risk.

Strong protections, recognition and service enforcement offset airport outing, custody isolation, healthcare bottlenecks and record anti-trans violence; functioning courts partially mitigate severe exposure for travellers.
